text:
Maria (SRE): heads up — getting multiple escalations from support: customers seeing sudden 429 bursts and occasional 502s after the rate-limiter config rollout at ~17:29 UTC. :rotating_light:

Sam (Support): seeing three separate customers with high error rates — most reports say it started right after the deploy. They send repeated retries and it just keeps 429-ing.

Sam (Support): example from customer A logs:
```
2026-03-15T17:31:05Z ERROR request_id=abc123 status=429 path=/v1/generate client=acme-inc tokens=34
2026-03-15T17:31:07Z ERROR request_id=abc124 status=502 path=/v1/generate client=acme-inc downstream_err="stream closed"
```

DeployBot: rollout completed: config-limiter-v2 (commit 9f4c2d) at 2026-03-15T17:29:10Z. Canary passed internal smoke at 17:25.

Devon (Runtime): I pulled the config. We changed burst handling: switched from per-client fixed token_buckets to a shared window counter + per-client burst allowance. Snippet from new config:
```
limiter:
  mode: shared_window
  window_ms: 1000
  refill_per_window: 50
  per_client_burst: 200
```

Maria (SRE): initial hypothesis: shared window math has an integer overflow/negative reset when window boundary crosses epoch second for high qps clients. That can cause buckets to be emptied incorrectly and then `X-RateLimit-Remaining` stays 0 for the next window until manual reset.

Tanvi (Oncall): I started a repro against staging with a req rate of ~1200/s from a single client id. Repro steps:
1) run: `for i in {1..2000}; do curl -s -H "X-Client-ID: repro-client" "https://staging.api.redwood.run/v1/generate" & done`
2) observe 429s spike at ~100th request and then persistent 429s for next ~2s.

Devon (Runtime): reproduced locally. See limiter log dump when boundary crossed:
```
[limiter] ts=1719999999 client=repro-client tokens=20 window_epoch=1719999 next_reset=-2147483648
[limiter] ts=1720000000 client=repro-client tokens=0 window_epoch=1720000 next_reset=-2147483648
```
That negative next_reset is suspicious — looks like signed int wrap.

Maria (SRE): agreed. Immediate mitigation options:
- rollback config to limiter-v1 (fast)
- hotfix limiter to clamp/reset on overflow and redeploy (safer)
- temporarily increase per-client burst to mask the issue (band-aid)

Devon (Runtime): patch ready: add saturating arithmetic and explicit window reset check. Patch diff:
```
- next_reset = compute_reset(window_epoch)
+ next_reset = max(0, compute_reset(window_epoch))
+ if next_reset < now: next_reset = now + window_ms
```

Tanvi (Oncall): I rolled the rollback to limiter-v1 at 17:38 UTC for prod. Observed error rates drop back to baseline in ~30s. :white_check_mark:

Sam (Support): customers reporting recovery. I'll close active escalations after validation.

Devon (Runtime): hotfix LGTM. I'll queue it for canary deploy after we finish a short postmortem. Plan: deploy patch to canary group (10% traffic) 17:55, monitor 10m, then staged rollout.

Maria (SRE): we should also adjust alerting — current alert fires on 5xx/429 rate but not on sudden sustained 429 with low server-side errors. Add an alert rule: if 429 rate > 5% for >60s and retries > 1000/min trigger P0. Also add an automatic rollback runbook link.

Devon (Runtime): noted. I'll add alert and create a synthetic test hitting shared-window edge case at 10-minute intervals.

Maria (SRE): action items:
- Devon: push hotfix + canary, add saturating checks and window clamping (owner)
- Tanvi: verify post-rollback telemetry and keep oncall for canary rollout (owner)
- Sam: follow up with customers and confirm closure (owner)
- Maria: write short post-incident note and link tickets (owner)

Sam (Support): I'll also add an internal KB entry with repro steps + recommended customer mitigation (backoff header suggestions) so CS can triage faster.

Devon (Runtime): canary results: 10m with canary traffic looked good, no sign of negative resets. Rolling to 50% now, will continue checking traces and `limiter.next_reset` metric.

Tanvi (Oncall): 50% -> 100% roll complete. Observed no recurring negative values. Latency back to normal, 429 rates at baseline. :tada:

Maria (SRE): good job. Postmortem outline: timeline, root cause = signed-int overflow in window reset math under high qps per-client with shared-window mode, short-term mitigation = rollback to limiter-v1, long-term fixes = saturating arithmetic, e2e synthetic test, alert changes, and deployment gating for limiter config changes.

Devon (Runtime): I'll open PR for tests and the patch is in prod. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/limiter/pull/345 (adding regression tests for window boundary case).

Sam (Support): customers A/B/C confirmed resolution and said ok to close tickets. I'll send a brief note with root cause summary and apology where needed.

Maria (SRE): leaving a follow-up checklist here to pick up tomorrow:
- ensure postmortem is published to incidents/ and shared with Support
- add a pre-deploy smoke in deploy pipeline that simulates 1k/s single-client burst against a canary limiter (Devon)
- ensure deploy runbook includes immediate rollback steps for limiter configs (Tanvi)

Tanvi (Oncall): I'll create the incident page and link the KB. Assigning timeline: postmortem draft by EOW.

Maria (SRE): thanks everyone. Closing thread but keeping follow-ups tracked in INC-2026-032 and PR link above. :eyes:
